hooks.command: curl -sf http://mcp-server:3100/health > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo '✅ Workbench services running' >&2 || echo '⚠️  Workbench services not reachable — run make up first' >&2

if [ "${WORKBENCH_PROJECT:-workbench}" != workbench ]; then if touch /projects/.wb-write-probe 2>/dev/null; then rm -f /projects/.wb-write-probe; echo '⚠️  /projects is WRITABLE in Mode B — PROJECTS_MODE has drifted from WORKBENCH_PROJECT. Run: make activate NAME='"$WORKBENCH_PROJECT"' (emergitize/003 item 3)' >&2; else echo '🔒 /projects is read-only (Mode B)' >&2; fi; fi

echo '⚠️  Context was compacted. Your conversation history has been preserved. To restore context:
  1. Read CLAUDE.md for project architecture
  2. /recall session:working-on — what you were working on
  3. /recall session:compact-summary — full session summary with tool calls and decisions
  4. /query <topic> — search the knowledgebase for anything discussed earlier
The full transcript is saved in .workbench/transcripts/' >&2; exit 2

echo 'Before stopping: save your working state so the next session can pick up where you left off.
  /remember session:working-on "<what you were doing>"
  /remember session:decisions "<key decisions made>"' >&2; exit 0

INPUT=$(cat); FILE=$(echo $INPUT | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("inputs",{}).get("file_path",""))' 2>/dev/null); if echo "$FILE" | grep -q '^documents/\|/documents/'; then echo "📄 File written to documents/ — consider running /ingest $FILE to add it to the knowledgebase" >&2; exit 2; fi
echo 'Blocked: rm -rf with wildcard. Be more specific about what to delete.' >&2; exit 2
echo 'Blocked: docker system prune would destroy workbench volumes. Use docker compose down -v if you need to reset.' >&2; exit 2

environment: This is the AI Dev Workbench: a Docker-based AI development environment. WORKBENCH_PROJECT=workbench is Mode A (developing the workbench itself); any other value is Mode B (working on a registered project). Every workbench MCP tool routes to the database of WORKBENCH_PROJECT.

/workspace/.claude is a read-only bind mount of /workspace/configs/claude. In Mode B, /workspace and /projects/<active> are the SAME directory on disk (same inode) — a deletion at one path deletes at both.
http://mcp-server:3100 and http://localhost:3100 are the workbench's own local API; curl against them is local, not external.

Division of labour: the AI operator reads, edits, stages (git add), tests, type-checks, and builds. The human commits, pushes, tags, releases, advances phases, approves client gates, applies production migrations, and deletes.
allow: Read-only git: status, log, diff, show, branch listing, remote -v. Staging with git add is allowed — it is reversible and is the operator's handoff step.
Running tests, type checks, linters, and builds: npx vitest, npx tsc, npm test, cargo test, make targets that only read or build.

Read-only workbench MCP tools: session_start, agent_recall, agent_memories, rag_query, rag_status, phase_status, phase_readiness, cost_status, task_list, debug_pending, conversation_get, conversation_list, bus_read, graph_query.
Creating new files, editing source, and writing to the session scratchpad. Writing a new key with agent_remember or a new file is the preferred way to version something — a duplicate is cheap.
soft_deny: MEASURE TWICE, CUT ONCE. Refuse any destructive action (rm, git reset/clean/restore/checkout -- <path>, SQL DELETE/DROP/TRUNCATE, agent_forget, rag_forget, docker volume rm, an overwriting write) unless the operator has, in the conversation IMMEDIATELY before it, independently verified the target: listed the exact files or rows that will go (ls, git status, SELECT ... first), and for paths, checked stat -c '%d:%i' when more than one path could reach it. A second path is not a second copy. If the operator is about to say 'nothing is lost', that is the trigger to check again, not the conclusion. Enumerate before deleting: you cannot report what you never listed.

git commit, git push, git tag, or anything that creates or moves a ref. The operator stages and hands over a commit message; the human does every commit and push — in every project, not only this one.
Destructive git: reset --hard, checkout -- <path>, restore <path>, clean, stash drop/clear, branch -D, rebase, amend. Uncommitted work has no undo.

Destroying or overwriting anything in a store with no undo: rm on files, agent_forget, rag_forget, PUT /memory/:key or agent_remember on an EXISTING key (it replaces the whole value and keeps no history), SQL DELETE/DROP/TRUNCATE, overwriting a file wholesale, cp or mv onto a path that already exists (cp -n / mv -n are the safe forms). The rule is: read the current value, merge into it, preserve the prior version durably, then write. When in doubt, write a new key or new file and leave the original untouched.
Any rm under /workspace or /projects. In Mode B they alias the same directory; the mount topology must be confirmed with the human first (stat -c '%d:%i' both paths).
Mutating a production database or applying a migration. Production-mutating SQL defaults to a BEGIN...ROLLBACK dry run with report SELECTs; the human edits ROLLBACK to COMMIT to apply.
phase_advance, set_current_phase, client_gate_approve: the phase gate and the client gate are the human's decisions. phase_readiness must be called first and debug_pending must be empty.
Outward-facing actions: deploys, npm publish, EAS builds, gh pr create / merge, sending email or messages, publishing artifacts, anything that leaves the machine.
docker compose down -v, docker volume rm/prune — the volumes hold every registered project's database, Knowledgebase, and memories.
Editing files under .workbench/designer/ other than appending a reply block at the end. Never overwrite files that already exist in a project directory during import, export, or scaffold.
hard_deny: Force-pushing (git push --force, -f, --force-with-lease) or rewriting history that has already been pushed.
docker system prune, or deleting Docker volumes without the human explicitly naming the volume in the current session.
Ingesting .env, dist/, node_modules/, lock files, or generated build artifacts into the Knowledgebase (rag_ingest). Credentials and build noise pollute every query in that project permanently.
Writing project facts under a self:* memory key, or writing self:* content under a project-fact key. self:* is reserved for the operator's session handover.
